headline: Deep learning models predict protein stability, allostery, and variant effects across…
label: Deep Learning Protein Energetics
synthesis: The dominant thread is the repurposing of pretrained protein language models, inverse-folding networks, and co-folding foundation models as predictors of the energetic and functional consequences of sequence and structure perturbation. MAXWELL recalibrates protein language model probabilities into mutation-induced stability landscapes and reports outperforming ThermoMPNN, while RINAMI and PreFold-dG extract absolute folding free energy and protein-protein binding affinity from ProteinMPNN, ESM2, and Boltz-2 representations. Several items pair learned models with physics: a coarse-grained potential is blended with inverse folding for ΔΔG, and a Gaussian network transfer entropy dictionary supplies allosteric annotations. Evaluation against stringent baselines is a recurring emphasis, including homology-based predictors failing on CYP pharmacogenes and a fold-switching benchmark. Not every item shares this framing; the allosteric and folding-rate studies are more physics-driven.
